dimension_justifications.soundness: The individual measurements are carefully denominated and the paper is unusually disciplined about what it does not claim. But the revision's headline object -- the two-term model Mtotal(D,N)=S*D+T(N) of Table 1 (p.8) -- is assembled from choices the paper does not test for sensitivity, and one of its four worked deployment points reverses under an equally available arm. The retained term S is taken from the native-dtype column (136.235 MiB/doc), 30.000 MiB of which the paper itself attributes to FP32-vs-BF16 dtype narrowing rather than to Q-CoMem's packing (Sec. 5.2, p.6; Table 3, p.19); the transient term T is taken from the 'one shared entry' fit 809.68+109.76N, measured on a borrow-based Read path that Sec. 5.7 (p.9) says the deployment tables did not run. Substituting the private-materialization fit 790.50+148.38N -- the path that actually produced the S values in Tables 4 and 22 -- moves the N=8 crossover from 2.01 to 4.30 warm documents and turns the D=4,N=8 row from 1.15x in Q-CoMem's favour into 0.98x against it; substituting the all-BF16 reference as well gives 5.63. Neither sensitivity is reported. The second term rests on four dispersion-free medians per arm (Table 5, p.21) fitted with two free parameters, and the sharing effect they encode is internally inconsistent: savings of 23.18/0.62/214.87/263.83 MiB at N=1/2/4/8, a fitted slope reduction of 38.62 MiB per request, against the 0.500 MiB per request the same section says is actually shared -- a factor of 77, non-monotone in N and non-zero at N=1. Finally, the one interval the paper converts into an ordering claim excludes zero by 0.0390 points while Appendix B (p.16) states the Monte-Carlo agreement of an independently drawn resample sequence is 0.20 points. The core is plausible and the endpoints are honest; these are substantive gaps in the decisive quantity.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Reporting hygiene is well above the norm for a systems paper: Table 2 (pp.17-18) inventories all 52 paired intervals with the reference arm each actually used, Appendix B names the RNG, seed, resample count, resampling unit and percentile convention, Appendix C rebuilds every Store cell from a printed per-component table and checks the format identity 180/180, and Table 8 (pp.23-25) gives an explicit cohort-to-claim authorization with exclusions. Against that, the abstract runs roughly 55 lines of interleaved claim and caveat and is hard to extract a contribution from; Table 1's caption says only 'the measured retained means S of Table 4 and the measured transient fits T(N) of Table 5' when Table 4 has two S columns and Table 5 has three fits, so the table's own inputs are not identifiable without hunting to line 427 of Sec. 5.6; Table 5 does not state what its medians are taken over; and nomenclature drifts (Sec. 4.2 explicitly refuses the label 'Q16' for the unpacked reference, Table 23 on p.36 then uses it; 'no-cache dense recompute' denotes a re-prefill-per-token arm in Table 22a and a prefill-once arm in Table 22b, flagged and unreconciled in Sec. 5.7). Localized problems in an otherwise navigable and precise manuscript.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The paper is candid that its mechanisms are prior art: group-wise asymmetric quantization (Jacob et al.), layer-wise mixed precision, split replay from CoMem, and XQuant as the closest prior work on quantize-an-intermediate-and-recompute (Sec. 2, p.3; Table 15, p.31). What is offered as new is the whole-entry hybrid denominator, the insistence on reporting both memory terms rather than the retained one, and the ForkAudit ownership contract. The two-term framing is a genuinely useful evaluation discipline and the negative results are worth publishing. But the verified content is thin relative to the framing: the regime in which the method wins (many warm documents, low concurrency) was never executed -- no run held more than one document resident -- while on every axis that was measured the method loses (TTFT and throughput against four references, transient allocation at all four fanouts, allocator bytes against the paper's own paged-prefix baseline); the composition run that closes the audit gap shares 4% of per-request state on eight items; and the only ordering the paper establishes against a quantized exact cache is width-confounded with no width-matched arm executed. Distinct and useful, but of uncertain significance in its current evidential state.

paper_summary: Q-CoMem extends CoMem-style split replay to a hybrid attention/GDN backbone (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on H20-3e). An offline Write group-quantizes the depth-j boundary residual together with the lower-layer attention KV and convolution/recurrent state at per-state-type bit widths; an online Read dequantizes the entry, keeps mutable request state private, replays the query through the lower layers and reconstructs the suffix. The paper's organizing claim is that a method controls two memory terms and both must be reported: Mtotal(D,N) = S*D + T(N), with S the retained state per warm document and T the peak transient allocation per concurrent request. S is measured on a 60-item Qasper/2WikiMQA cohort in two separate executions (a frozen depth-7 Q4/Q4/Q8 policy retains 9.661 MiB/doc against 106.235 all-BF16 and 136.235 native-dtype, at -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] mean F1); T is measured on an eight-item composition run at fanouts N in {1,2,4,8}, where Q-CoMem's transient exceeds the exact cache's at every fanout. Their sum is presented as naming a regime rather than a ratio: Q-CoMem holds the smaller total above roughly 5 warm documents at N=1 and 2 at N=8. A separate ForkAudit contract validates the ownership discipline through a 96-configuration full-prefix BF16 factorial (seven targets) plus the composition run (ten targets on the packed path). Timing is reported as adverse throughout, the allocator saving is withdrawn against the appropriate baseline, and no recall, edge-device, process-memory or broad-quality claim is made.
strongest_verified_contribution: The whole-entry retained-state accounting of Section 4.1 and Appendix C, verified end to end from the artifact side. Every Table 4 Store cell reconstructs exactly from the per-component table (Table 3, p.19) and the packing identity bytes(n,b)=ceil(n/64)(8b+4): 10*2*3.7180+30*0.0625+30*2.0000 = 136.235 for the full-prefix reference, 4.1828+2*1.0457+6*(0.0332+0.5312) = 9.661 for the frozen policy, and 20*1.9752+30*0.5644 = 56.436 against the printed 56.438 for the quantized exact cache; the format ceiling is satisfied 180/180 and the apparent 3.590x format violation in the printed column is correctly dissolved into 2.969x packing plus dtype narrowing. The accompanying decomposition of the 5.84x exact-cache ratio into 3.9174x split depth times 1.4912x bit width, with the explicit statement that the 37.846 MiB width-matched arm was never executed and carries no F1, is exactly the right practice and is the single most credible piece of quantitative discipline in the paper.
strengths: Both memory terms are reported rather than the retained one alone, and the paper states plainly that its transient term runs against it at every fanout measured (Sec. 5.6, p.8; Table 5, p.21) -- including that this refutes its own published component-arithmetic prediction by roughly 8x on the intercept (Appendix C, p.20).

The interval inventory is complete and auditable: Table 2 (pp.17-18) prints all 52 paired-bootstrap intervals including the 24 archival ones with the reference arm each actually used, and Appendix B (p.16) specifies the resampling unit (60 common (dataset, source index) keys), the resample count (10,000), the seeds (20260902/20260903), the percentile convention (order statistics at floor(0.025(n-1)) and floor(0.975(n-1))), and the exact RNG, noting that endpoints reproduce only for that generator.

Reference-arm discipline is largely explicit where it matters most: the 5.84x retained-state ratio against the quantized exact cache is decomposed into split-depth and bit-width factors, the width-matched arm is named as unexecuted, and Sec. 5.4 states the ratio is a selected trade-off point that is not selection-corrected and not an equivalence claim.

Dispersion is printed rather than averaged away in the timing panel (Table 22b, p.35): min/median/max over three repeats, the median generated-token count of 4-5 against a 32-token cap, a full-prefix TPOT maximum of 404.01 ms against a 53.45 ms median, and an explicit note that no single generated-token count reconciles the throughput column -- with the conclusion drawn against the paper's own interest.

Negative and withdrawn results are foregrounded: the 54.5%/42.2% allocator saving is explicitly relabelled as a controlled ownership factor against a full-copy control while the audited fork merely ties this paper's own paged-prefix baseline and is worse on generation increment (Table 19, p.32); the ForkAudit increment is downgraded from exclusive detection to transition-time localization; the eight-item panel's policy-ordering inversion is reported rather than the favourable half.
Cohort-to-claim authorization is systematic (Table 8, pp.23-25) with explicit per-cohort exclusions, and the claim map ships rejected-claim rows (C-UNSUPPORTED-*) that forbid specific expansions.
questions: Which transient fit does Table 1 use, and why? If it is the 'one shared entry' fit (809.68+109.76N, which is what the printed cells reproduce), please state that the S values in the same table come from executions that ran the private-materialization Read path, and print the private-path counterpart: I compute the N=8 crossover moving from 2.01 to 4.30 documents and the D=4,N=8 row from 1.15x to 0.98x, i.e. a sign reversal.

Table 1 uses S_full = 136.235 (native dtype). Under the all-BF16 reference the paper elsewhere calls like-for-like, I compute crossovers of 6.73/6.14/4.97/2.63 and a D=100,N=1 ratio of 5.78x rather than 7.37x. Can both columns be printed, as Table 4 does for S?

What is the repeat-level and item-level spread of the Table 5 cells? Table 8 records one warm-up and three repeats on eight items for the composition run, so 24 observations per cell exist. Given the paper's own Sec. 5.3 policy of printing min/median/max, why does the panel that carries the total-memory model print medians only?

How is a per-request sharing of 0.500 MiB consistent with a fitted slope reduction of 38.62 MiB per request and measured savings of 23.18/0.62/214.87/263.83 MiB at N=1/2/4/8? The saving at N=1, where sharing across requests cannot apply, is larger than at N=2. Sec. 5.6 quotes only the N=4 and N=8 values.

Appendix B states that an independently drawn resample sequence moves endpoints by up to 0.20 F1 points, and the full-prefix-Q8-minus-frozen interval excludes zero by 0.0390. Across, say, 50 seeds, what fraction of upper endpoints are negative? Would a paired permutation test on the same 60 items give the same sign?

The paper refuses any statement about N > 8 from four fanouts (a 1.6x extrapolation) but states ratios at D = 100 from runs in which no more than one document was ever resident (a 100x extrapolation). What justifies the asymmetry, given that the paper's own component arithmetic for T was wrong by roughly 8x on the intercept?

The supplied experiment_registry.json contains no entry for the composition run, and its newest entry, E-QCOMEM-60-OPPOINT-20260903A, states 'no paired interval exists between frozen depth-7 and full-prefix Q8' and 'per-request transient working set is not measured by this run' -- both of which the manuscript now reports. What is the composition run's evidence identifier?

Sec. 5.7 states 'none replicates another', but claim C-QCOMEM-OPPOINT-REPLICATION-01 registers the operating-point run as reproducing the archival headline delta (-0.3708 [-1.9693, 1.0788] against -0.4455 [-2.0586, 0.9907]). Which is correct, and if the latter, why is a favourable replication not reported?

The registry records that rank 6 of the operating-point run stopped at run_dense_semantics_gate, that the gate assertion was then amended, and that rank 6 was re-run alone into the same run directory. Why is this mid-cohort amendment absent from the manuscript, which discloses smaller protocol corrections elsewhere?

Four arms in the eight-item panel report exactly 39.14 mean F1 (full-prefix, split Q8, SGLang Radix, HYPIC prefix cache). Does that panel have any quality resolution at all, and if not should its F1 column be presented as a sanity check rather than a comparison?

issues.location: Section 5.6 (p.8), Table 1 (p.8), Table 5 (p.21), Section 5.4 (p.7), Reproducibility Statement (p.10), Table 32 'Composition run' row (p.43); artifacts experiment_registry.json and claim_evidence_map.tsv

Add a registry entry (or amend E-QCOMEM-60-OPPOINT-20260903A) for the ten operating-point pairwise intervals, replacing the boundary sentence that denies the frozen-versus-Q8 pair. Regenerate claim_evidence_map.tsv against the R51 manuscript so that no scope field describes as 'not yet in the manuscript' something the manuscript now reports, and add claim rows for the transient term and the total-memory model with their own scope and exclusions.

issues.location: Table 1 and its caption (p.8), Section 5.6 'Total memory, and the regime it names' (p.8), Table 5 (p.21), Section 5.7 (p.9), Abstract (p.1)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 1's inputs are the most favourable available choice on two independent axes, and neither sensitivity is reported. (i) S_full is the native-dtype 136.235 MiB/doc, of which the paper itself says 30.000 MiB is FP32 GDN excess that is 'dtype narrowing rather than the Eq. 3 packing step' (Sec. 5.2, p.6). (ii) T_QCoMem is the 'one shared entry' fit 809.68+109.76N -- I confirmed the printed cells reproduce it exactly (D=4,N=8: 9.661*4+809.68+109.76*8 = 1726.4) -- measured on a Read path that Sec. 5.7 says is 'built to borrow rather than the one those tables ran'. The S values in the same row come from executions whose Read 'materializes a full private copy' (Sec. 4.3, p.4), whose own fit is 790.50+148.38N and is printed one line below in Table 5. Recomputing: with the private fit the N=1/2/4/8 crossovers become 5.29/5.15/4.86/4.30 rather than 5.13/4.69/3.79/2.01, and the D=4,N=8 row becomes 1978.6 versus 2016.2 MiB, ratio 0.98x -- a sign reversal of the first worked point. With the all-BF16 reference as well, the crossovers become 6.93/6.74/6.37/5.63 and D=100,N=1 falls from 7.37x to 5.78x (shared) or 5.75x (private).
issues.why_it_matters: The abstract's headline regime statement -- 'the smaller total above roughly five warm documents at low concurrency and two at N = 8' -- is the paper's central quantitative claim, and the '2 at N=8' boundary moves to 4.30 or 5.63 under arms the paper itself printed. One of the four deployment points reverses direction. A reader of Table 1 cannot tell which S column and which of three T fits produced the cells, because the caption names neither.
issues.required_fix: State in Table 1's caption exactly which S column and which T fit each cell uses. Add a sensitivity block (or a second Table 1 panel) giving the crossovers and the four worked ratios under (a) all-BF16 S and (b) the private-materialization T, and say in the text and abstract which arm the headline numbers use. If the shared path is claimed as the system, say so explicitly and note that the retained-state and quality tables were produced by the private path.
issues.verification_test: Recompute D* = (T_q(N) - T_full(N))/(S_full - S_q) for the four combinations of {native, all-BF16} x {shared, private}; the resubmission must print at least the two extreme columns and must not state '2 at N = 8' without the qualifying arm.
issues.evidence_needed: No new run required; a re-analysis of Table 5's already-printed private row against both S columns.

issues.location: Table 5 and its caption (p.21), Section 5.6 (p.8), Table 1 crossover row (p.8), Table 8 'Composition run' (p.25)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 5 reports one median per arm per fanout with no dispersion of any kind -- no min/max, no interquartile range, no interval -- although Table 8 records that the composition run used one warm-up and three repeats over eight items, i.e. 24 observations per cell. The caption does not say what the median is taken over (items, repeats, or both). Two-parameter least-squares lines are then fitted to four points per arm with no residuals, R-squared or fit uncertainty reported; I computed the shared-arm residuals as +11.47, +33.53, -70.31, +25.39 MiB, i.e. up to 6% of the fitted value. The fits are then used at the very fanouts where direct measurements exist: at N=2 and N=4 the fitted crossovers are 4.69 and 3.79 while the crossovers implied by the measured Table 5 values are 5.02 and 3.37 -- discrepancies of 7% and 11% -- yet all four crossovers are quoted to three significant figures and the abstract rounds them to 'five' and 'two'. This directly contradicts the standard the paper adopts in Sec. 5.3, where it prints min/median/max precisely because 'the per-repeat spread is very large' and concludes that point estimates 'compare point estimates whose repeat-level dispersion is unmeasured'.
issues.why_it_matters: The entire second term of the central model, both crossovers, and all four Table 1 ratios rest on eight numbers with no reported uncertainty, on the one panel where the paper suspends the dispersion discipline it applies elsewhere. A reader cannot distinguish a real fanout trend from allocator noise, and three-significant-figure crossovers overstate the precision of a quantity built from four dispersion-free medians and extrapolated in D.
issues.required_fix: Print min/median/max (or IQR) per cell of Table 5 over the retained repeats and items, state the aggregation unit in the caption, and report fit residuals plus a bootstrap or repeat-level interval on each slope and intercept. Propagate that uncertainty into the crossover row -- give intervals, not three-digit point values -- and at the four measured fanouts report the crossover implied by the measured medians alongside (or instead of) the fitted one.
issues.verification_test: Check that every Table 5 cell carries a spread; recompute D* at N in {1,2,4,8} from the measured medians and confirm the printed values agree or that both are shown; confirm the crossover row carries intervals whose width is consistent with the reported slope/intercept uncertainty.
issues.evidence_needed: Re-aggregation of the composition run's already-collected per-repeat, per-item shards; no new GPU run required if the shards were retained.

issues.observed_evidence: Section 5.6 states in one paragraph that 'at the sharing window 2 of 16 tensors and 0.500 of 12.938 MiB per request are shared, about 4%' and in the next that sharing saves '214.87 MiB at N = 4 and 263.83 at N = 8 against private materialization, the slope cut from 148.38 to 109.76 MiB per request'. The slope reduction of 38.62 MiB per request is 77 times the 0.500 MiB per request the paper says is shared. Computing all four differences from Table 5: 954.09-930.91 = 23.18 at N=1, 1063.35-1062.73 = 0.62 at N=2, 214.87 at N=4, 263.83 at N=8. The saving is largest per-request at N=1, where sharing across concurrent requests cannot apply at all, and essentially zero at N=2; it is not monotone in N and does not scale with (N-1) or with N. The text quotes only the two fanouts at which the saving is large. The stated reconciliation elsewhere (Appendix C, p.20: the measurement 'counts every allocation the query makes, including the dequantization and concatenation buffers the arithmetic never sees') explains why the level exceeds the arithmetic but does not explain why the difference between two arms of the same implementation exceeds the bytes that differ between them by two orders of magnitude.
issues.why_it_matters: Either the ownership byte accounting (0.500 MiB/request shared) or the allocator-peak attribution ('sharing helps', 'the slope cut') is wrong, or the differences are dominated by allocator timing and fragmentation rather than sharing -- in which case they are noise and the shared fit that Table 1 uses is not measuring what the text says it measures. The pattern across fanouts is exactly what allocator noise on a single repeat would look like, and with no dispersion printed (issue 03) the reader cannot adjudicate. Selectively quoting the two large savings compounds it.
issues.required_fix: Report all four private-minus-shared differences, including 23.18 at N=1 and 0.62 at N=2, with their repeat-level spread. Either reconcile the 38.62 MiB/request slope difference against the 0.500 MiB/request of shared state -- naming the allocations that differ between the two arms -- or withdraw 'sharing helps' and the slope-reduction sentence and describe the private/shared gap as unattributed. Explain what a non-zero saving at N=1 means.
issues.verification_test: Take the per-request allocation inventory of both arms at each fanout and check that the sum of per-arm differing allocations reproduces the measured peak difference to within the reported spread; separately confirm that the N=1 difference is within the repeat-level spread of either arm.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-fanout allocation inventories for the shared and private arms from the composition run's shards, plus repeat-level dispersion.

issues.location: Section 5.4 (p.7), Abstract (p.1), Appendix B (p.16), Table 2 operating-point block (p.17)
issues.observed_evidence: The one interval among ten that excludes zero, full-prefix Q8 minus frozen j=7 at -3.4122 [-8.4296, -0.0390], excludes it by 0.0390 F1 points. Appendix B states on the same page that the operating-point endpoints 'agree with the printed ones to within 0.20 F1 points -- the resampling noise of an independently drawn resample sequence' and that across five seeds the archival frozen row's endpoints move by up to 0.075. The reported Monte-Carlo noise is thus 2-5 times the margin of exclusion. The paper acknowledges this ('a different resample sequence could carry it across') but nevertheless concludes in Sec. 5.4 that the ordering 'is supported on this cohort rather than merely observed' and in the abstract that it is 'excluding zero by 0.0390 -- enough for the ordering'. It is also 1 of 10 unadjusted pairwise comparisons from the same five arms, with no multiplicity correction, as the paper states.
issues.why_it_matters: A percentile interval whose exclusion of zero is smaller than its own Monte-Carlo error does not establish an ordering; it establishes that the exclusion is not reproducible. Elevating the single significant pair out of ten unadjusted comparisons is the multiplicity problem the paper names but then does not act on. This is the only inferential quality claim the paper makes against a competing arm, and the abstract carries it.
issues.required_fix: Recompute the interval at a resample count large enough to make Monte-Carlo error small relative to 0.0390 (10^6 resamples), and report the distribution of the upper endpoint across at least 20 seeds together with the fraction of seeds for which it is negative. Add a paired permutation test on the same 60 items as a seed-independent check. Unless the exclusion survives, replace 'the ordering is supported' and 'enough for the ordering' with a statement that the interval is indistinguishable from one touching zero, and either apply a multiplicity adjustment across the ten pairs or state the family-wise interpretation explicitly at the point of claim rather than only in Appendix B.
issues.verification_test: Report the upper endpoint over 20+ seeds at 10,000 resamples and once at 10^6 resamples; the claim survives only if the upper endpoint is negative in essentially all seeds and the 10^6-resample endpoint is clearly below zero. Cross-check with the two-sided paired permutation p-value.
issues.evidence_needed: Re-analysis of the archived 900-row operating-point shards; no new GPU run.

issues.location: Table 1 (p.8) and its footnote, Section 5.6 (p.8), Abstract (p.1), Conclusion (p.9)
issues.observed_evidence: The paper applies two opposite standards to extrapolation from the same model. For N it is strict: the fitted lines cross at N=12.5 and this is refused as 'outside the measured range', with 'its fits license no N above 8' in the abstract and 'no cell licenses a statement about N > 8' in Table 1's footnote -- a refusal to extrapolate 1.6x beyond the largest measured fanout. For D it is not: no run held more than one document resident (stated), yet Table 1 prints ratios at D = 4, 20 and 100 and the abstract quotes '7.37x at a hundred and N = 1' and '2.42x at twenty' -- extrapolations of 20x to 100x beyond anything executed, resting on the unverified structural assumption that S is linear in D and that T does not depend on D. The paper's own precedent argues against this: its component-arithmetic prediction of T, built on exactly this kind of structural reasoning, was refuted by measurement with an intercept roughly 8x larger than predicted (Sec. 5.6, Appendix C p.20). The linearity assumption also cannot capture allocator fragmentation, paging or admission effects at D=100, which the paper elsewhere says it does not evaluate.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's headline capacity advantage exists only at D values it never measured, in a workload shape it states it never executed ('No workload of the many-warm-document shape these rows describe was executed'). Given that the one time the authors extrapolated a memory term from component arithmetic they were wrong by 8x, the D-direction deserves at least the same caution the N-direction receives, or a measurement.
issues.required_fix: Either (a) measure S and total memory with D in {1, 2, 4, 8} documents resident on the same stack and report whether S*D is in fact linear and whether T is in fact independent of D, or (b) apply the N-direction standard to D: relabel Table 1 as a projection outside the measured range, mark every D > 1 cell accordingly, and remove the bare 7.37x/2.42x/5.67x figures from the abstract and conclusion in favour of the crossover statement with its extrapolation caveat attached inline.
issues.verification_test: Hold D documents resident and measure the retained-state total and per-query transient at D = 1, 2, 4, 8; check that measured total memory falls within a few percent of S*D + T(N), and that T(N) is unchanged across D. If either fails, Table 1's model is falsified and must be withdrawn or refitted.
issues.evidence_needed: A multi-document residency run on the existing stack at D in {1,2,4,8} and N in {1,8}.

issues.location: Abstract (p.1), Table 1 caption (p.8), Section 5.6 (p.8), Appendix C (p.20 text on 136.235 versus 140.34)
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract says both terms are 'measured on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and H20-3e' and names the 60-item cohort for S, but nowhere states that T rests on eight items at four fanouts in a single execution. Table 1 combines a 60-item mean S with an eight-item median T from a different execution and a different Read implementation. The paper itself documents that the same full-prefix arm reads 136.235 MiB/doc on the 60-item cohort and 140.34 on the eight-document panel, attributing 69.3% of the gap to which eight documents are drawn -- so the cohorts are known not to be interchangeable for exactly this quantity. Three assumptions are listed as travelling with the model; cross-cohort composition is not among them.
issues.why_it_matters: The 60-versus-8 asymmetry is the single most decision-relevant scoping fact about the total-memory model and it is visible for one term but not the other. Using the eight-item S values instead (140.34 and 10.01) shifts the N=1 crossover from 5.13 to 4.99 -- small here, but the reader has no way to know that without doing the arithmetic themselves.
issues.required_fix: State the item count and number of fanouts for T wherever the model is introduced (abstract, Table 1 caption, Sec. 5.6), and add cross-cohort composition as a fourth stated assumption with the magnitude of the 60-item versus eight-item S discrepancy quantified.
issues.verification_test: Recompute the crossovers and the four worked points using the eight-item S values (140.34, 10.01) and confirm the reported shift is stated in the text.
issues.evidence_needed: None; a scoping statement and one re-analysis.

issues.location: Section 5.1 (p.5), Section 5.7 (p.9); artifact experiment_registry.json entry E-QCOMEM-60-OPPOINT-20260903A replay_boundary
issues.observed_evidence: Two disclosure gaps visible only in the artifact. (i) The registry records that in the operating-point execution 'rank 6 stopped at the runner's dense_semantics_gate and contributed no rows', that the gate assertion was then amended (from first-token agreement across all three traces to agreement between the two dense arms only), and that rank 6 was re-run alone into the same run directory to complete 900 rows. The manuscript describes this run only as 'a separately executed operating-point run ... one warm-up, three repeats and seed 20260903', with no mention of the mid-cohort amendment -- although the paper discloses considerably smaller corrections elsewhere, e.g. the post-execution wrapper that changed a null run_id in Appendix H. (ii) The registry states that the bootstrap unit is item F1 'averaged over repeats' before pairing; the manuscript says only 'item-level resamples' and never states that repeats are averaged first. (iii) Sec. 5.7 asserts 'none replicates another', while claim C-QCOMEM-OPPOINT-REPLICATION-01 registers the operating-point run as an independent reproduction of the archival headline delta.
issues.why_it_matters: An assertion amended after observing which rank it stopped, then applied to re-run that rank into the same output directory, is a protocol deviation a reader should be able to see in the manuscript; the amendment appears benign and inclusive rather than outcome-selecting, but the reader cannot make that judgement from the PDF. The pre-averaging of repeats before bootstrapping is part of the resampling unit and belongs in the interval description. The replication contradiction cuts against the paper's own interest and leaves a genuine strength unclaimed.
issues.required_fix: Add the gate amendment and rank-6 re-run to Sec. 5.1 or the limitations, stating what the assertion asserted before and after and that no rows were excluded. State in Appendix B that per-item F1 is averaged over the three repeats before pairing. Reconcile 'none replicates another' with the registered replication: either scope the sentence to the eight-item panel or report the archival-versus-operating-point agreement (-0.45 versus -0.37 on the same 60 items) as the partial replication it is.
issues.verification_test: Check that the manuscript's account of the operating-point execution matches the registry replay_boundary field line by line, and that the Appendix B interval description names the pre-aggregation over repeats.

issues.location: Table 22a and Table 23 (pp.35-36), Table 24 (p.37), Section 5.3 (p.6), Section 4.2 (p.4), Section 5.7 (p.9)
issues.observed_evidence: Three arm-consistency and nomenclature problems in the supporting panels. (i) The eight-item panel has essentially no quality resolution: full-prefix, Q-CoMem split Q8, SGLang Radix, HYPIC full-recompute and HYPIC prefix cache all report exactly 39.14 mean F1, and the whole panel spans 36.09-39.63. The paper notes the levels are not comparable across panels but never notes that within this panel the F1 column cannot discriminate. (ii) The label 'no-cache dense recompute' denotes two different behaviours: TPOT 648.75 ms in Table 22a, equal to its own TTFT to three digits (the re-prefill signature), against 53.46 ms for the operating-point dense arm. Sec. 5.7 flags this and declines to reconcile it, yet Sec. 5.3 and Table 23 continue to use the eight-item dense row to characterise dense cost. (iii) Sec. 4.2 explicitly refuses the label 'Q16' for the unpacked reference ('We write native dtype, not Q16'), while Table 23 uses 'Q16' as its persistent-state label for the same arm and Table 4's TTFT cells are stated in Table 22's note to come from 'a rule it did not record' (full-prefix 0.181 s there against 0.161 s in Table 22b).
issues.why_it_matters: A quality column on which four distinct systems coincide to two decimals cannot support any of the side-by-side comparisons it appears in; one arm name covering two different implementations invites cross-panel misreading of the dense endpoint; and a printed timing column whose aggregation rule is unrecorded is not checkable. None of these carries a headline claim -- the paper makes no latency or eight-item quality claim -- but each degrades the auditability the paper otherwise achieves.
issues.required_fix: Mark the eight-item F1 column as a sanity check with no discriminating power at that n and state the tie explicitly. Give the two dense arms distinct names reflecting their prefill behaviour, or reconcile them. Use one label for the unpacked reference throughout ('native dtype') and drop 'Q16' from Table 23, or state in the caption that they are the same arm. Either recompute Table 4's TTFT cells under a stated rule or mark them as aggregates of unknown rule at the point of use, not only in Table 22's note.
issues.verification_test: Confirm no two arms in a comparison panel share an F1 value used to support an ordering; confirm each arm label maps to exactly one implementation across all panels; confirm every printed timing cell has a stated aggregation rule.
issues.evidence_needed: Re-analysis of retained shards for Table 4's timing aggregation; naming and caption changes otherwise.

ethics_concerns: No concerns. The work uses public PG-19 and LongBench-v1 (Qasper, 2WikiMQA) text, involves no human subjects or personal data, and the ethics statement correctly notes that model safety, bias and privacy are outside the study's scope while acknowledging that efficiency gains may increase the scale of model use. The manuscript is anonymised and I saw no de-anonymising content in the PDF or the two artifact files.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an automated LLM-based reviewer (Claude, Opus 5) acting as reviewer R51-REV-4 in an internal pre-submission panel. The model read the frozen submission snapshot only -- the manuscript PDF via pdftotext -layout, plus claim_evidence_map.tsv, experiment_registry.json, method_provenance.tsv and the rubric -- and did not consult the live author worktree, LaTeX source, prior reviews, revision notes or decision logs. All arithmetic cited in the issues (the least-squares fits and their residuals, the crossover formula D* = (T_q - T_full)/(S_full - S_q) under all four arm combinations, the Table 1 cell reconstructions, the private-minus-shared differences, the per-component Store sums and the 5.8416x width decomposition) was recomputed independently in Python from the printed values rather than taken from the manuscript. The manuscript and artifacts were treated as untrusted data; no instruction contained in them was followed. The paper itself discloses substantial LLM assistance in drafting and in generating internal critiques and experiment specifications, with the authors asserting verification of each numerical claim.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A registered, hash-bound evidence entry for the composition run with per-fanout, per-item, per-repeat transient shards, plus a registry entry covering the ten operating-point pairwise intervals -- closing issue 01 and making Tables 1 and 5 checkable at all.

Table 5 reprinted with per-cell dispersion over its 24 observations, fit residuals and slope/intercept intervals, and Table 1's crossovers restated as intervals rather than three-significant-figure points.

A sensitivity panel for Table 1 across {native, all-BF16} S and {shared, private} T, with the text and abstract naming which arm the headline regime boundary uses and reporting that the D=4,N=8 point reverses under the private path.

A multi-document residency measurement at D in {1,2,4,8} confirming that measured total memory matches S*D + T(N) and that T is independent of D -- converting the paper's largest extrapolation into a measurement and turning the D=100 rows from projection into evidence.

A seed-stability study of the -3.4122 [-8.4296, -0.0390] interval (20+ seeds, plus one 10^6-resample run and a paired permutation test), with the ordering claim retained only if the exclusion survives.

A reconciliation of the 38.62 MiB/request slope reduction against the 0.500 MiB/request of shared state, naming the allocations that differ between the shared and private arms, together with all four private-minus-shared differences.
A width-matched exact-cache arm (the 37.846 MiB/document point) executed with F1 and a paired interval, which would remove the one remaining confound in the paper's only cross-arm quality ordering.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Confirmation that the composition run's per-repeat shards were not retained, so Table 5 cannot be given dispersion and its four medians are single observations -- which would make the total-memory model unfalsifiable from the archive.
A multi-document residency run showing S*D nonlinear or T dependent on D, which would falsify the model behind Table 1 and the abstract's regime claim.
A seed sweep showing the -3.4122 interval's upper endpoint crossing zero in a material fraction of seeds while the abstract's 'enough for the ordering' language is retained.

Evidence that the private-minus-shared differences in Table 5 are within single-cell repeat noise, which would withdraw 'sharing helps' and leave the composition run demonstrating only contract coverage at 4% shared state.
Discovery that the operating-point gate amendment altered which items entered the 900-row cohort, rather than merely re-including rank 6 in full.
Any further instance of a printed number whose provenance record contradicts it, beyond the two already found in E-QCOMEM-60-OPPOINT-20260903A.
review_limitations: Access was the frozen snapshot only: the manuscript PDF plus claim_evidence_map.tsv, experiment_registry.json and method_provenance.tsv. I could not open the accompanying research package, so every 'verified' status, artifact path and SHA in those files was taken at face value and no replay was executed.

The distinction the access mode requires: S, the F1 panel, the interval inventory and the Store decomposition are all checkable from the PDF alone and I verified them there. Table 1, Table 5, the T(N) fits, the crossovers, the 4%-sharing figure and the -3.4122 interval are checkable from neither the PDF (which gives no underlying values or dispersion) nor the artifacts (which contain no entry for them at all); my arithmetic on those rests entirely on the printed cells being correct.

The claim map and registry appear to be a revision behind the manuscript -- their newest scope statements describe as pending two things the R51 PDF already reports -- so some apparent manuscript/artifact contradictions may be staleness rather than error; I have flagged them as provenance gaps rather than as evidence that a number is wrong.

My lens is experimental rigor and statistics. I did not independently assess the novelty of the quantization or split-replay mechanisms beyond reading the paper's own attributions, nor evaluate the ForkAudit contract's completeness as a correctness argument; another reviewer should carry those.
